briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for November 1, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Direct Threats of Climate Change and Warnings on Safety
sections.content: Over the past five years, 1,054 flights in Korea have been diverted due to climate change, leading to an emergency in airport safety measures [1]. This is a clear example demonstrating that climate change is directly impacting our daily lives and infrastructure. Internationally, natural disasters and climate change are increasing the threat of invasive species to Pacific islands, raising concerns about ecosystem disruption and community safety [15]. These phenomena warn that climate change is no longer a distant future problem but a severe, ongoing threat.

sections.title: 🌍 Conclusion of COP17 Biodiversity Convention and Challenges for the International Community
sections.content: The CBD COP17 meeting concluded with the adoption of the 'Yerevan Pathway' and completed the first 'global review' to reverse nature loss by 2030 [4, 20]. While an agreement was reached at this meeting to strengthen nature conservation and funding, concerns were simultaneously raised that it was a 'fragile agreement' and that countries would fail to meet their nature targets [18, 19]. Critics pointed out that the current system could hinder progress, emphasizing the urgent need for practical implementation and systemic reform to halt nature destruction [19].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Implementation Efforts and Technology Innovation Trends
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to address climate change are ongoing. The Gimhae Research Institute hosted a forum on industrial transition and supply chain response in the era of climate change, while Haenam County is exploring ways to respond to climate change and utilize robot technology for the future of agriculture [2, 3]. Seoul National University's 'Carbon Neutrality Hall' has been established, drawing attention as a potential hub for achieving carbon neutrality, and in Incheon, the Carbon Neutrality Implementation Task Force held a discussion forum to expand citizen participation and discuss nine practical tasks [5, 6, 8]. Furthermore, there are calls for the introduction of 'reduction-aware budget statements' to enhance the effectiveness of local governments' carbon neutrality efforts, and the utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology in responding to the climate crisis is also being actively explored [7, 9].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Growth Prospects for Eco-Friendly Industries
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy is driving the growth of related industries. Several markets, including wire ferrules, distribution boards, and Belleville washers, are projected to leverage renewable energy as a primary growth driver until 2035 [10, 12, 13]. Notably, the renewable energy production from buildings that underwent Seoul's architectural review over the past five years has amounted to 1.5 times that of a thermal power plant, indicating significant achievements in renewable energy adoption within the urban construction sector [14]. Gyeongsang National University's ETP also held a renewable energy workshop in Jeju, examining the energy transition efforts for a 'carbon-free island,' demonstrating comprehensive efforts towards clean energy transition [11, 17].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, while the threat of climate change persists, both domestic and international policy efforts and technological innovations are actively underway to overcome it. Emphasizing once again the importance of climate action, this concludes today's climate briefing.
